name: Wildflower seeds
description: A mix of small meadow-flower seeds. Quick to sprout in open, sunny ground.

facts.text: Mature wildflowers drop fresh seed, so one patch can become many.

name: Moss spores
description: Fine dust gathered from established moss. Settles best on damp, shaded ground.

facts.text: Moss has no seeds or flowers; it spreads by spores and fragments.

name: Fern spores
description: Spores shed from the undersides of mature fern fronds.

facts.text: Fern spores need moisture to grow into new ferns.

name: Grass seeds
description: Seed heads from ornamental grasses. Hardy and unfussy.

name: Maple samaras
description: Winged maple seeds that spin as they fall. Patience turns one into a tree.

facts.text: The paired wings of a samara slow its fall so the wind can carry it.

name: Rush cuttings
description: Young shoots of soft rush, ready to settle into wet ground at the pond's edge.

name: Twigs
description: Small fallen branches. The backbone of most natural shelters.

facts.text: Old trees and overgrown corners are the best places to find twigs.

name: Bark
description: Loose strips of bark shed by old trees. Good for roofing a shelter.

facts.text: Many beetles shelter under loose bark.

name: Stones
description: Weathered garden stones, some still carrying patches of moss.

facts.text: Stone arrangements give small creatures cool, sheltered crevices.

name: Leaf litter
description: Fallen leaves and needles. Keeps a shelter damp and snug.

facts.text: Leaf litter slowly breaks down into rich soil.

name: Bamboo shoots
description: Young shoots lifted from the edge of a bamboo clump, ready to start a new one.

facts.text: New bamboo culms reach their full height in a single season.

name: Bamboo canes
description: Light, strong, hollow canes cut from mature bamboo.

facts.text: Hollow canes make ideal nesting tubes for solitary bees.

hints.text: Mature bamboo can be harvested.

name: Forest grass divisions
description: Small clumps split from Japanese forest grass, each ready to root.

facts.text: Forest grass spreads slowly by short underground stems.

name: Hosta divisions
description: A crown of hosta, divided with its roots, waiting for a shady spot.

facts.text: Hostas are grown for their leaves, but their tall flower spikes feed bees.

name: Maple leaves
description: Fine, deeply cut leaves from a mature Japanese maple, glowing red and orange.

facts.text: Fallen leaves make soft, insulating nest linings.

hints.text: A fully grown maple may yield something new.

name: Maple sap
description: A little clear, faintly sweet sap that weeps from a mature maple.

facts.text: Some butterflies, like the red admiral, feed on tree sap as well as nectar.

hints.text: A fully grown maple may yield something new.

name: Seed bundle
description: Spare seeds wrapped in leaves and tied with grass: a store of food that draws insects and birds to a shelter.

facts.text: Seed heads left standing feed birds and shelter insects through the lean months.

name: Water lily rhizomes
description: A knobbly root of water lily, ready to sink into pond mud.

facts.text: Water lilies root in the mud and send their leaves up to the surface.

name: Reed rhizomes
description: A length of creeping reed root with a fresh shoot.

facts.text: Reeds spread along the margin by creeping roots.

name: Hornwort sprigs
description: Feathery sprigs of a pond plant that lives wholly under water.

facts.text: Hornwort has no roots; it drifts in deeper water.

name: Reed stems
description: Dry, hollow reed stems, light and easy to weave.

facts.text: Bundled reed stems make shelters and screens.

hints.text: Mature reeds shed stems you can gather.

name: Clay
description: Smooth grey clay from the pond banks.

facts.text: Clay holds water, which is why the old pond still has its shape.

hints.text: Clearing the overgrown banks may turn up clay.

name: Lichen fragments
description: Crusty flakes of lichen that will take hold on bare stone.

facts.text: A lichen is a fungus and an alga living as one.

name: Thyme cuttings
description: Fragrant sprigs of creeping thyme, ready to root.

facts.text: Thyme roots easily from a sprig pressed into dry soil.

name: Fescue seeds
description: Fine seeds of a tough blue-grey grass.

facts.text: Fescues thrive where the soil is thin and dry.

name: Dwarf pine seedling
description: A tiny pine in a ball of gritty soil.

facts.text: Dwarf pines grow only a few centimetres a year.

name: Gravel
description: Pale, rounded gravel from the old stone garden.

facts.text: Raked gravel stands for water in many Japanese dry gardens.

hints.text: Clearing the stone garden’s overgrowth turns up gravel.

name: River stones
description: Smooth, water-worn stones, grey and speckled.

facts.text: Stones warm in the sun and hold the heat into the evening.

hints.text: Old river stones lie hidden under the stone garden’s overgrowth.

name: Royal fern spores
description: Green spores from the tip of a royal fern frond.

facts.text: Royal ferns carry their spores on special upright fronds.

name: Wood sorrel seeds
description: Tiny seeds that pop from wood sorrel’s pods.

facts.text: The ripe pods flick their seeds a surprising distance.

name: Mushroom spawn
description: Threads of fungus in a handful of damp sawdust.

facts.text: A mushroom is only the fruit; the fungus lives as threads in the wood.

name: Deadwood
description: Old, softening branches from the woodland floor.

facts.text: Decaying wood is home to more life than living wood.

hints.text: Fallen wood lies hidden under the hollow’s overgrowth.

name: Leaf mould
description: Dark, crumbly earth made from rotted leaves.

facts.text: Leaf mould holds water like a sponge and feeds the soil.

hints.text: Leaf litter left to rot in a bed becomes rich leaf mould.

name: Clover seeds
description: Tiny kidney-shaped seeds of white clover.

facts.text: Clover enriches poor soil as it grows.

name: Oxeye daisy seeds
description: Fine dark seeds from a dried daisy head.

facts.text: One daisy head holds hundreds of seeds.

name: Aster seeds
description: Light, tufted seeds of a late-flowering aster.

facts.text: Aster seeds drift away on little parachutes.

name: Bellflower seeds
description: Dust-fine seeds shaken from a bellflower pod.

facts.text: Bellflower seeds need light to sprout.

name: Meadow grass seeds
description: A mix of tall meadow grass seed.

facts.text: Tall grasses give meadow insects shelter.

name: Seed heads
description: Dry flower heads full of ripe seed.

facts.text: Left standing, seed heads feed birds through the winter.

hints.text: Meadow flowers shed seed heads once they have flowered.

name: Grass stems
description: Long, dry meadow grass stems.

facts.text: Dry grass stems are used to thatch and to weave.

hints.text: Tall meadow grass sheds dry stems.

name: Iris seeds
description: Flat brown seeds from a Japanese iris pod.

facts.text: Irises grow best with their feet in wet ground.

name: Sedge divisions
description: A rooted clump of streamside sedge.

facts.text: Sedges have triangular stems: “sedges have edges”.

name: Marsh fern spores
description: Spores of a fern of wet, shaded banks.

facts.text: Marsh ferns spread by creeping roots along wet ground.

name: Pebbles
description: Small round stones, smoothed by the stream.

facts.text: The stream rolls pebbles smooth over many years.

hints.text: The stream’s overgrown banks hide smooth pebbles.

name: Cherry sapling
description: A young flowering cherry, a whip of a tree with a few buds.

facts.text: Flowering cherries are grafted to keep their blossom true.

name: Camellia cuttings
description: Glossy-leaved cuttings of camellia.

facts.text: Camellias flower in the cold months when little else does.

name: Azalea cuttings
description: Small-leaved cuttings of satsuki azalea.

facts.text: Satsuki azaleas flower in early summer, a month after others.

name: Hydrangea cuttings
description: Soft cuttings of a lacecap hydrangea.

facts.text: Its flower colour changes with the soil.

name: Quince cuttings
description: Thorny cuttings of flowering quince.

facts.text: Flowering quince bears small, fragrant fruit after its blossom.

name: Blossom petals
description: Soft pink petals, fallen from the cherry.

facts.text: Falling blossom is celebrated in spring across Japan.

hints.text: The old cherry drops petals as it flowers.

name: Quince fruit
description: Small, hard, golden fruit with a sweet scent.

facts.text: Birds come for it in autumn.

hints.text: Flowering quince fruits once it has flowered.

name: Holly berries
description: Red berries of Japanese holly, each with a hard seed.

facts.text: Birds carry holly seeds through the woods.

name: Ivy cuttings
description: Trailing cuttings of ivy, rooting at every joint.

facts.text: Ivy flowers late, when few other plants do.

name: Wood anemone roots
description: Thin brown roots of wood anemone.

facts.text: It flowers before the canopy fills with leaves.

name: Acorns
description: Glossy acorns from the ancient oak.

facts.text: Many woodland creatures depend on acorns in autumn.

hints.text: The ancient oak drops acorns.

name: Fallen branches
description: Sturdy branches brought down by the wind.

facts.text: Old trees shed branches as they age, making new homes for wildlife.

hints.text: The canopy floor hides fallen branches under its overgrowth.

name: Cattail shoots
description: A rooted shoot of cattail, ready for the mud.

facts.text: Cattails spread through the mud by thick roots.

name: Marsh marigold divisions
description: A clump of marsh marigold with glossy leaves.

facts.text: One of the first flowers of the year in wet places.

name: Frogbit buds
description: Small winter buds of frogbit, which float up in spring.

facts.text: Frogbit buds sink in autumn and rise again in spring.

name: Cattail fluff
description: Soft, downy fluff from a ripe cattail head.

facts.text: Birds line their nests with cattail fluff.

hints.text: Ripe cattails shed soft fluff.

name: Japanese apricot sapling
description: A young ume tree, its buds already fat.

facts.text: Ume blossom opens in late winter, before any other tree.

name: Beautyberry cuttings
description: Arching cuttings of Japanese beautyberry.

facts.text: Its violet berries cluster along the stems in autumn.

name: Mondo grass divisions
description: A clump of dark evergreen mondo grass.

facts.text: Mondo grass stays green all winter.

name: Snowdrop bulbs
description: Small white bulbs that flower in the depths of winter.

facts.text: Snowdrops push up through frozen ground.

name: Beautyberries
description: Glossy violet berries, beloved of winter birds.

facts.text: Birds strip the stems bare by midwinter.

hints.text: Beautyberry fruits in autumn.

name: Evergreen sprigs
description: Dark sprigs of mondo grass and other evergreens.

facts.text: Evergreens give a garden its shape in winter.

name: Lotus rhizomes
description: A long, jointed lotus root, ready for the pond mud.

facts.text: Lotus seeds can wait in the mud for centuries before sprouting.

name: Weeping cherry sapling
description: A young weeping cherry, its slim branches already falling.

facts.text: Weeping cherries are among the most treasured trees in old gardens.

name: Fine timber
description: Seasoned, straight-grained timber from the garden’s old buildings.

facts.text: Old garden pavilions were built without nails.

hints.text: The Noble Garden’s overgrowth hides old timber.

name: Ornamental stones
description: Shaped and dressed stones from the garden’s old paths and bridge.

facts.text: Stones were chosen for their shape and set with great care.

hints.text: Dressed stones lie buried under the Noble Garden’s overgrowth.

name: Black bamboo shoot
description: A shoot of black bamboo, given in thanks for the restored grove.

facts.text: Rare: it comes only from completing restoration stages.

name: Bamboo deer-scarer
description: A keepsake from restoring the garden. Place it from Build, under Features.

facts.text: Its gentle knock marks the passing of time in the garden.

name: Pink lily rhizome
description: A rhizome of pink water lily, given in thanks for the restored pond.

facts.text: Rare: it comes only from completing restoration stages.

name: Frog stone
description: A keepsake from restoring the garden. Place it from Build, under Features.

facts.text: Frog stones are said to bring good fortune home again.

name: Cushion moss clump
description: A small dome of cushion moss, given in thanks for the restored stone garden.

facts.text: Rare: it comes only from completing restoration stages.

name: Snow-viewing lantern
description: A keepsake from restoring the garden. Place it from Build, under Features.

facts.text: Its broad roof is made to hold a cap of snow in winter.

name: Painted fern spores
description: Spores of the painted fern, given in thanks for the restored hollow.

facts.text: Rare: it comes only from completing restoration stages.

name: Mossy stump
description: A keepsake from restoring the garden. Place it from Build, under Features.

facts.text: Rotting wood like this is a whole world for small creatures.

name: Gentian seeds
description: Fine seeds of the Japanese gentian, given in thanks for the restored meadow.

facts.text: Rare: it comes only from completing restoration stages.

name: Straw bee skep
description: A keepsake from restoring the garden. Place it from Build, under Features.

facts.text: Solitary bees nest in the hollow stems of its straw.

name: Primrose seeds
description: Seeds of the Japanese primrose, given in thanks for the restored stream.

facts.text: Rare: it comes only from completing restoration stages.

name: Bamboo water pipe
description: A keepsake from restoring the garden. Place it from Build, under Features.

facts.text: Birds come to drink and bathe at its trickle.

name: Tree peony cutting
description: A cutting of tree peony, given in thanks for the restored court.

facts.text: Rare: it comes only from completing restoration stages.

name: Blossom-viewing bench
description: A keepsake from restoring the garden. Place it from Build, under Features.

facts.text: Made for the old custom of sitting to watch the blossom fall.

name: Golden-rayed lily bulb
description: A bulb of the golden-rayed lily, given in thanks for the protected canopy.

facts.text: Rare: it comes only from completing restoration stages.

name: Stone bird bath
description: A keepsake from restoring the garden. Place it from Build, under Features.

facts.text: Birds bathe to keep their feathers in good order.

name: Egret orchid tuber
description: A tuber of the egret orchid, given in thanks for the restored marsh.

facts.text: Rare: it comes only from completing restoration stages.

name: Reed screen
description: A keepsake from restoring the garden. Place it from Build, under Features.

facts.text: Small birds use it as a windbreak on cold days.

name: Sasanqua cutting
description: A cutting of sasanqua camellia, given in thanks for the four-season garden.

facts.text: Rare: it comes only from completing restoration stages.

name: Moon-viewing platform
description: A keepsake from restoring the garden. Place it from Build, under Features.

facts.text: Moon viewing is an autumn custom, but the moon rises every season.

name: Butterfly maple seedling
description: A seedling of the butterfly maple, given in thanks for the restored Noble Garden.

facts.text: Rare: it comes only from completing restoration stages.

name: Moon gate
description: A keepsake from restoring the garden. Place it from Build, under Features.

facts.text: Stepping through a moon gate is said to bring a fresh start.
